clue.text: People that routinely take drugs tests and steal the supply

definitions.text: People that routinely take drugs tests

indicators.note: read as supple-ly, i.e. flexibly, so the words before it are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of swiping the stock of drug-testing kits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun meaning stock, but here it is an adverb from supple: the letters of STEAL THE are bent into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Competitive sportspeople are routinely subjected to doping tests, so they are the people who regularly take them.

clue.text: Bottom bird lifted up to use premises

parts.note: ass is the American word for the backside

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the word up means reading it from bottom to top

parts.note: the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: A bird's backside is raised so it can use some premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted up' reverses EMU to UME in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppose something is to take it as a starting point for argument, a premise.

clue.text: Leader's temper makes contribution to grave situation

parts.note: a head is a leader, with the 's kept as S
to temper something is to tone it down, so temper gives tone as a noun of character or mood

explanation.surface: A boss's bad mood makes a serious situation worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave situation' reads as a crisis, but it means a situation at a grave in a churchyard.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved memorial stone is set up at a burial plot, so it is part of the scene at a grave.

clue.text: Learned on-line technology, like Yahoo, say, is taking over

parts.note: E is short for electronic, as in e-mail and e-commerce

indicators.note: the outer word takes over, i.e. swallows, the inner one

parts.note: a yahoo is a coarse, boorish person in Swift's Gulliver's Travels, so like one is rude
IT stands for information technology

explanation.surface: An online firm like Yahoo is taking over, educated in internet technology.
explanation.walkthrough: Yahoo reads as the internet company, but the clue means a boor, from Swift's Gulliver's Travels; 'taking over' means the outer word swallows the inner one.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholarly and widely read, someone learned has great erudition.

clue.text: Age when he's beginning to deal with growing up

indicators.note: in a down clue, growing upward means the letters are read from the bottom
the beginning of the word he's is just its first letter

parts.note: to cope is to deal with something

explanation.surface: Age is when a young man starts to handle growing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growing up' turns H plus COPE, HCOPE, upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An era or long period of history is an age.

clue.text: American society on school run …

indicators.note: in an across clue, US and S coming on SCH means they follow it

parts.note: US is short for United States, hence American

explanation.surface: A US society organises the school run, leading into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'school run' is the British daily drive taking children to school; here 'run' is a ski run, and the ellipsis carries on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight, fast downhill ski descent is a kind of run on the slopes.

clue.text: Spooner's renting property that cannot be surpassed

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for a noun: the limit above which nothing goes

indicators.note: Rev. Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the initial sounds are exchanged

parts.note: together with the next word, renting property is leasing; its first sound is the LEA part
the rest of leasing, the SING part, whose opening S sound is swapped

explanation.surface: Someone's lettings business owns a building nobody can top.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds L and S in 'lea-sing' to get 'sea-ling', which is said the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An upper limit, such as a price cap, is a level that cannot be exceeded.

clue.text: Loose woman, relatively speaking, is relieved of her top

indicators.note: her top is the first letter of the word for the woman, which is taken away

parts.note: a woman described as a relative is an aunt, here the familiar form

explanation.surface: A promiscuous female relative is stripped of her top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose woman' reads as one phrase, but 'Loose' is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To loose a knot or bond is to unfasten it.

clue.text: Ran with no cover on inside bet

indicators.note: the word for on is placed inside the word for bet

parts.note: to stake money is to bet it
RE means on or about, as in business letters

explanation.surface: Someone ran unprotected after placing a bet on the inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no cover' suggests no shelter or insurance, but means without clothes: running naked through a public place.
explanation.definitionFit: Running naked in public, typically at a sports match, is a prank with no clothing covering the runner.

clue.text: … in chaos as fun gets out of hand

definitions.note: used as an adjective here, meaning chaotic

indicators.note: letters thrown into chaos are jumbled

explanation.surface: Following the previous clue, a school run descends into chaos as the fun gets out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to the school run, but this clue stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Military slang for a muddle (situation normal, all fouled up), used to describe things gone chaotic.

clue.text: Reveal suit with 40% cut in charges here

definitions.text: Reveal suit with 40% cut in charges here

parts.note: to out someone is to reveal their secret
to fit is to suit, as clothes that fit you suit you

indicators.note: cut means letters are trimmed away, and the 40% before it says how many: two of the five

parts.note: terms are prices or fees, as in reasonable terms

explanation.surface: A tailor's shop shows suits with 40% knocked off the prices.
explanation.walkthrough: '40% cut' leaves TER from TERMS by removing two of its five letters. The whole clue also describes the shop: suits are sold there and it charges you.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothing shop selling suits and kit is one that charges for its goods; the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Suspect fault provides case for court using discretion

indicators.note: the jumbled letters form a case around the abbreviation
suspect as an adjective means dubious, signalling the letters are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: A suspected fault gives grounds for a lawsuit, handled discreetly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suspect' looks like a verb but is the adjective meaning dubious; 'provides case for' has the jumbled letters (TAFUL) wrap around the court abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomatic, discreet person handles delicate matters with sensitivity and discretion.

clue.text: She aims to change one who's expected to deliver

indicators.note: the letters are made to change their order

explanation.surface: A woman sets out to change things as the person everyone counts on.
explanation.definitionFit: A promised saviour awaited by believers is expected to deliver, i.e. save, his people.

clue.text: Agree with artist creating monstrous image using animal parts

parts.note: to chime with something is to agree with it
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Someone agrees with an artist who is making a grotesque picture from animal bits.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the fire-breathing monster had a lion's head, goat's body and serpent's tail.

clue.text: This rather reflects on you

parts.note: a reflexive pronoun reflects back on the subject, and the formal 'one' stands in, rather, for 'you'

explanation.surface: Something here reflects badly on the person spoken to.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a reproach; grammatically it is the reflexive form of the indefinite pronoun, which can be used instead of yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: This reflexive pronoun is a formal stand-in for yourself and turns the action back on the speaker.

clue.text: Shops publicise work Serpent reviewed

indicators.note: viewed again backwards, i.e. read in reverse

parts.note: to air an opinion is to make it public
OP is short for opus, a work
the setter's pseudonym, so the setter is me

explanation.surface: Stores promote the latest output from Serpent, which has been critiqued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' looks like criticism but reverses AIROPME.
explanation.definitionFit: Large stores or marketplaces, the Latin plural of a trading centre.

clue.text: Struggle to find revealing yet sturdy underwear?

definitions.meaning: to fumble about searching, as in the dark
a G-string made sturdier, string being upgraded to rope

explanation.surface: Someone fumbles for a skimpy but robust piece of lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a joke: a G-string is skimpy, and a stronger string would be rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel about blindly for something is to struggle to find it.

clue.text: Subtle meaning suggested by public figures?

definitions.note: singular phrase for a plural noun of implied meanings

parts.note: overt means open and public
ones are figures, i.e. digits

explanation.surface: A hint drawn from what celebrities do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'public figures' reads as celebrities, but it splits into public and figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Implications or connotations conveyed beneath the surface of what is said.

clue.text: Sell when one's expected to maintain tense and bitter disagreement

parts.note: to vend is to sell

indicators.note: to maintain something is to hold it, so ETA holds the letter

parts.note: ETA, estimated time of arrival
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A seller arriving keeps things tense in a bitter row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when one's expected' is a roundabout way of saying estimated time of arrival; 'to maintain' means hold, so the tense letter goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running feud is a bitter, often violent quarrel between parties.

clue.text: Arms go inside openings of each sleeve

indicators.note: the word for go is placed inside the first letters
the openings of words are their first letters

parts.note: to go is a euphemism for urinating, to pee

explanation.surface: Arms are pushed through the openings of each sleeve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arms' look like limbs, but they are weapons; 'go' is the toilet euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: Fencing swords are weapons, and weapons are arms.

clue.text: Fresher American soldiers rise up

definitions.note: sassy, meaning cheeky, is chiefly American usage

parts.note: the SAS, Special Air Service, is a regiment of soldiers

indicators.note: up can mean in disorder, as in things being up in the air, so the word is jumbled

explanation.surface: Newer US troops stage an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American soldiers' looks like one unit; 'American' belongs to the definition, flagging the American word, and 'up' jumbles RISE to SIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh can mean cheeky or impudent, and the American word for more impudent is this comparative.

clue.text: Artistic board's sense of taste discerned by audience

indicators.note: what an audience discerns is what it hears, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: the palate is the sense of taste

explanation.surface: An artistic committee's taste is judged by the public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artistic board' reads as a committee but means a painter's mixing board.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter mixes colours on a thin board held in the hand.

clue.text: Leading character in The Passion on stage

indicators.note: the leading character of a word is its first letter

parts.note: heat is passion, as in the heat of the moment
RE means on or about, as in business letters

explanation.surface: The lead role in a Passion play on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading character' sounds like a starring role but means the first letter of The.
explanation.definitionFit: Drama as a profession or art is often called the stage.

clue.text: Introduction to qualification comprises Derrida's articles on what limits semiotics

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: Jacques Derrida was French, and un and le are French articles, indefinite and definite

indicators.note: the limits of a word are its outer letters

explanation.surface: An academic primer on semiotics, drawing on Derrida's papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' look like academic papers but are grammatical articles in French; 'what limits' takes S and S from semiotics.
explanation.definitionFit: This conjunction introduces a condition or proviso, i.e. a qualification of a statement.

clue.text: Cabinet position with responsibility for clothing company

definitions.meaning: a piece of furniture with shelves and cupboards

definitions.text: position with responsibility for clothing company
definitions.meaning: a theatre job helping the cast, the company, into costume

explanation.surface: A cabinet post that oversees a clothing firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet position' reads as a ministerial post, and 'company' as a business; it is an acting troupe.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen sideboard is a type of cabinet; in theatre, the dresser helps actors into their costumes.

clue.text: Makes accommodation for those who aren't quick verbally

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the word becomes another of the same sound

parts.words: accommodation for those who aren't quick
parts.note: the quick are the living, so those not quick are the dead, housed as ashes in urns

explanation.surface: Someone provides facilities for slow learners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quick' means alive, as in 'the quick and the dead'; in a non-rhotic British accent URNS and the answer sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To make money is to be paid it as income.

clue.text: Counter intelligence describing support to enhance deal

indicators.note: counter means running the opposite way, so the letters are read backwards
to describe a shape around something is to enclose it

parts.note: news is intelligence, i.e. information
a golf tee supports the ball

explanation.surface: Counter-intelligence agents back an operation to improve a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter intelligence' reads as spy work, but 'Counter' reverses everything after 'describing' wraps the golf peg in the word for intelligence, giving NETEEWS before the turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To make an offer more attractive by adding an inducement improves the deal.

clue.text: Week early in month passed quickly

indicators.note: the letter goes in near the start of the month's abbreviation

parts.note: Sept is short for September

explanation.surface: A week at the start of a month flew by.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rushed or flew past moved by rapidly.

clue.text: Period home had come to an end

parts.note: a term is a period of time
in means at home
to have a meal is to eat it, so had gives ate

explanation.surface: The school term at home had finished.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop or finish is to conclude, ending something.

clue.text: Unit measuring weight put on neural nets

indicators.note: nets means catches, so the run of letters is caught within the words

explanation.surface: A weighting unit applied to a neural network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nets' looks part of 'neural nets', but is a verb meaning catches.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric measurement of mass equal to a thousand kilograms.

clue.text: Guarantee that's equally reliable

parts.note: as means equally, as in as good
sure means reliable, as in a sure thing

explanation.surface: A promise that is just as dependable.
explanation.definitionFit: To promise someone confidently is to give a guarantee, a verb sense.

clue.text: The first to split up when they're unfaithful

definitions.note: a clause standing for a plural noun: people without faith

indicators.note: the inner letters split the outer word into two parts

parts.note: as means when, as in as I left
1ST, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: The first to break up when partners cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfaithful' suggests cheating partners but means lacking religious faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbelievers have no religious faith, so they are literally without faith.
